Check all components and the app for available updates
Choose which components RHI checks for updates. Components you turn off are not checked during startup or Update All.

When On, RHI silently installs component updates in the background after each update check. Games that are running when an update is detected are updated once they close. Does not apply to app updates.
Swaps games to the newest DLSS when a new version is released. Only affects games on the previous latest version; older versions you picked yourself are left alone.
Swaps games to the newest Streamline when a new version is released. Only affects games on the previous latest version; older versions you picked yourself are left alone.
Closing the window keeps RHI running in the system tray.
Right-click the tray icon or pinned taskbar icon to quickly launch recent games.
Creates a scheduled task that launches RHI with elevated privileges, so there is no prompt each time. Takes effect after RHI restarts.
The drop helper window enables Discord drag-and-drop in admin mode. Disable if you don't need it. Restart required.
Paste a GitHub Personal Access Token (PAT). It stays valid until you revoke it. No scopes needed, just generate and paste.
Remove the saved token.
Sign out of GitHub.
RHI Database uses the community-maintained RHI database (recommended). RenoDX Wiki falls back to the RenoDX wiki scraper. Changing this setting triggers an immediate refresh.

When On, each game gets its own screenshot subfolder.
Controls how shaders are displayed in the ReShade overlay. Tabs groups effect files into named tabs; Tree shows a collapsible hierarchy.
Writes the overlay key, screenshot key, screenshot folder and effect list style into every game's reshade.ini. Skips hidden games and games set to keep their own reshade.ini.
Your monitor's peak brightness in nits, written to reshade.ini presets. Press Enter to save.

RHI Managed: deploy built-in shader packs to all games.
Custom: use your own shader directory.
Off: RHI never touches shaders on any game.
When On, all shader packs are downloaded and cached at startup. When Off, packs are downloaded on demand when needed.
RHI watches this folder for RenoDX addon files (.addon64/.addon32) and archives. Defaults to your Downloads folder.
Pick the folder RHI watches for addon downloads
Go back to your Downloads folder
When On, Windows HDR is automatically enabled when launching a game through RHI and disabled when the game exits.
Select which monitors to enable HDR on. Empty = primary display only.
When On, switches to the target resolution on game launch and restores it on exit.
Select which monitors to change resolution on.
Desktop resolution to switch to before a game launches. Restored on game exit.
Select which display to configure.
Bits per colour channel sent to the monitor. 10 bpc or higher suits HDR. Only depths your monitor and cable support will work.
Full suits PC monitors. Limited suits TVs that expect video levels. The wrong one makes blacks look grey or crushed.
Apply the colour depth and dynamic range to the selected monitor.
Adjust NVIDIA Digital Vibrance (color saturation) per-display. Saved values are automatically restored on app startup.
How to use DLDSR Control
Adjust DSR smoothness (0-100%). Lower values are sharper, higher values are smoother. ~15 second display blackout on apply.
Apply the selected smoothness value. Causes ~15 second display blackout.
Select a previously captured DLDSR state to apply.
Apply the selected DLDSR state. Causes ~15 second display blackout.
Capture the current DLDSR state from NVIDIA Control Panel. Configure DLDSR in NVIDIA CP first, then capture.
Delete the currently selected saved state.
Refresh the current DLDSR state from registry.
Choose the DLSS / Streamline versions, presets and render scales that Quick Apply uses.
Controls the DLSS text overlay NVIDIA shows in the corner of games. Global system setting — affects all games. Requires admin.
Global DMFG max frame count. Games using Dynamic mode inherit this unless overridden per-game.
Global DMFG target frame rate. Off = no target. Max Refresh Rate = match display. Or pick a specific FPS.
Deploy DLSS and Streamline DLL versions and DLSS presets to multiple games at once. Backs up originals automatically. Pre-populated with your configured defaults.
Global VSync mode — applies to all games without a per-game override.

Global FPS cap via NVIDIA driver. VRR-optimal presets cap just below refresh rate to stay in VRR range. Choosing a cap also turns the per-game FPS limit Off for every game with ReLimiter or Display Commander, so the two limiters don't fight.
Globally enables or disables G-Sync/FreeSync variable refresh rate.
Controls G-Sync/FreeSync variable refresh rate. Fullscreen and Windowed recommended for seamless experience.
Shows NVIDIA's G-Sync indicator in games when G-Sync is active. Global driver setting, affects all games.
Highest available forces your max refresh rate. App Setting lets games choose their own refresh rate.
Global power management mode — applies to all games without a per-game override.
Maximum disk space for compiled shader cache. Larger = fewer stutters on revisits. 16GB is the driver default.
Auto-compiles shaders in the background when idle. Higher = more CPU usage during idle, faster first-time game loads.
Global Resizable BAR — enables large GPU memory transfers for all games. Requires admin and compatible hardware (RTX 30 Series+).
Maximum BAR transfer size. 1GB is optimal for most games. Decrease to 512MB if experiencing ReBAR-related stutters.
Creates NVIDIA driver profiles for all games that don't have one yet. Games without a profile don't get the driver defaults above (Power Mode, VSync and so on).
Save all per-game NVIDIA profile settings to a backup file. Useful before updating drivers.
Restore per-game NVIDIA profile settings from a previous backup.
Removes ALL per-game NVIDIA profile overrides. The global profile will be like new.
Deletes the NVIDIA DXCache and GLCache folders. Forces shaders to recompile on next launch.
The key that toggles the ReLimiter OSD overlay in-game.
Global FPS cap written to all relimiter.ini files. Select a VRR preset or Custom for a manual value.
When On, all games share the same OSD presets file. When Off, each game has its own presets.
Shows DLSS quality mode, render resolution, and active features on the ReLimiter OSD. Disable if experiencing crashes.
Writes the overlay key, Shared presets, DLSS hooks and Target FPS into every game's relimiter.ini. Skips hidden games.
The GPU brand in this PC. RHI uses it to pick which OptiScaler.ini to install. DLSS inputs appears for AMD and Intel.
On: OptiScaler reports an NVIDIA GPU to the game, so the game offers DLSS and OptiScaler uses its inputs. Off: no GPU spoofing. Used when OptiScaler.ini is installed.
The key that opens the OptiScaler overlay in game. Saved straight away for new installs; use the button to update games that already have OptiScaler.

Clears all caches and re-scans everything from disk. Use as a last resort if games are missing, paths have changed, DLSS has been added to a game, or the DLSS section is missing from a game card.
Deletes cached DLSS, Streamline, and component staging files to free disk space. Shaders, installed addons, and version metadata are preserved. Files are re-downloaded automatically when needed.
